newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia joins GSM mobile phone network.
newsitem.headline: Serbia joins GSM mobile phone network.

text.p: Serbia on Thursday joined the global mobile telephone network by launching the first GSM (Global System for Mobile communications) exchange.

The GSM operator for Serbia MOBTEL -- a joint venture between Serbia's PTT and Braca Karic, a private company -- opened the GSM exchange for commercial traffic. The exchange was equipped by Ericsson of Sweden.
This is the third phase of developing mobile telephony in Serbia, said a statement issued by MOBTEL.

"Today Serbia opens its door to the world," Ilija Stojanovic, a member of the Serbian Academy of Arts and Sciences, said at a ceremonial opening of the exchange, attended by senior representatives of Ericsson management.

"This is a historical moment for Serbia. Today we deliver a digital cellular GSM system of mobile telecommunications...one of the last true technological miracles of the 20th century," Serbian PTT general manager Milorad Jaksic said.
The first phase of developing mobile telephony in Serbia started in Belgrade with installation of 11 basic stations and 36 transmitters. The system now covers 4,600 subscribers.
Another step envisages installation of nine additional stations in Belgrade, while another 16 stations would cover the Subotica--Belgrade-Nis stretch.
By installing 77 new transmitters by mid-November the system would encompass 17,000 subscribers.
MOBTEL plans to install a total of 68 stations and 338 transmitters for 60,000 subscribers by the end of 1996.
In January 1997 the system will be enlarged by another 10,000 subscribers.
The first mobile phone system entered Serbia in 1995 with a launch of the analogue NMT system while in February 1996 a pilot GSM exchange was put into a trial run.
